areas_of_law: Tax litigation / Tax Court of Canada procedure
issues: Whether a reply's pleaded assumptions that recite evidence, argument, or characterizations rather than material facts should be struck
Whether pleading unproven allegations of fraud or illegality as 'assumptions' improperly shifts the burden of proof onto the taxpayer
Whether allegations concerning the conduct and internal affairs of third parties are relevant and properly pleaded in a reply
Whether settlement payments, interest and legal fees paid without any judicial finding of wrongdoing are deductible as business expenses under the Income Tax Act
Whether a legal theory that expenses are non-deductible where conduct is 'egregious or repulsive', absent a finding of wrongdoing, is so untenable as to be struck at a preliminary stage
Whether the requirement that pleaded facts (not evidence or argument) be included in a reply has been breached
What the appropriate remedy is where a reply mixes proper assumptions with improper argument and evidentiary detail (strike whole reply vs. particular paragraphs vs. leave to amend)
key_facts: Client is a large Canadian financial institution acting through foreign affiliates
Affiliates participated in structured financing transactions with an energy company that later collapsed in an accounting scandal
Client was named in a securities class action and in claims by the bankruptcy estate, both settled for billions
No court ever made a finding that the client did anything wrongful
Client deducted settlement payments, interest, and legal fees as business expenses
Minister denied the deductions and reassessed
Crown's reply in the Tax Court appeal exceeds 80 pages, with roughly 70 pages of pleaded assumptions
Assumptions characterize the financings as 'disguised loans' and assert the client knowingly aided fraud and falsified financial statements
Reply recites conduct/internal affairs of the energy company and other third parties, quotes U.S. pleadings, and names dismissed employees
Crown's theory is that 'egregious or repulsive' conduct bars deduction regardless of income-earning purpose
causes_of_action: Tax Court of Canada appeal from reassessment (deductibility of business expenses)
Motion to strike portions of the Crown's reply / motion for particulars
candidate_statutes: Income Tax Act (Canada), s. 18(1)(a) and s. 18(1)(b)
Tax Court of Canada Rules (General Procedure)
